name: Azariah
overview: Azariah was a male Levite who served as the chief priest of the house of Zadok, a significant priestly lineage in Israel. His role as chief priest placed him in a position of religious leadership and responsibility within the tribe of Levi. No additional personal notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Azariah means 'YHWH has helped,' reflecting a divine assistance theme common in Hebrew names. This proper name is noted in 2 Chronicles 31:10 and was not given directly by God but carries a meaningful declaration of God's support.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Azariah was a descendant of Zadok, linking him to a prominent priestly family. Beyond this, no further family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Azariah's importance lies in his priestly leadership as chief priest of the house of Zadok, emphasizing the continuity of faithful priestly service in Israel. His position underscores the vital role of the Zadokite priests in maintaining proper worship and temple duties. His life, connected to the broader narrative of faithful service and God's provision, illustrates the necessity of honoring God's holiness through established priestly lines.
